title: Symplectic model projectors, parametrices and solvability
source_hypothesis: Scalar finite-contact model D_r+i*r^k*D_t, every integer k>=1, n>=2, both parity and frequency cases. Higher-dimensional microlocal mapping and solvability require nonzero last covector. Variable-coefficient transfer uses the full classical FCM normal form; arbitrary-regularity nonsolvability is asserted at positive simple-bracket characteristics.
reviewed_arguments: The scalar model retains every k>=1, both parity cases, all dimensions and the exact positive/negative frequency convention. The higher-dimensional Sobolev assertion explicitly requires a nonzero last covector.

The distributional graph operator is closed and compact smooth functions are an actual graph core, by spatial cutoff and coefficient-controlled mollification. Both adjoint domains and every rough null solution are determined.

Coercivity extends to the closed domain. The Hilbert projection argument, closed range and exact adjoint kernel construct the bounded minimal inverses; all unbounded adjoint identities are justified on the graph domain.

The even-contact signed integral inverse gives the exact locally integrable complex kernel. Abel regularization specifies its distributional extension and the logarithmic integrability bound excludes an extra diagonal distribution.

The odd-contact inverse removes the exact weighted moment. Its cumulative density and both tail estimates give uniform kernel bounds, including zero frequency, and identify the formula with the minimal inverse.

The Fourier integrals are actual distributions. Plancherel gives orthogonal projections, every inverse identity and both annihilation equations; the input transposes retain the correct opposite Fourier covector.
Projection wavefront containment uses all base derivatives, common characteristic equations and the exact frequency sign. Divergence on an explicit nearby diagonal path proves equality.

The inverse kernel has only the diagonal relation by favorable hypoellipticity in either the output or transposed input variables. The forcing identity and closedness prove equality, including all axis exclusions.
A complete localized Fourier kernel argument proves action on compact distributions, seminorm continuity, wavefront composition and extension of test-function identities by common polynomial bounds.

The tangential estimate treats low frequencies by the actual compact input/output kernel bound, rather than a divergent square of the global inverse estimate. High frequencies retain the exact fractional gain.

The ordinary conic comparison works for every real Sobolev order, including negative orders. Full two-dimensional mapping follows from the complementary elliptic estimate and a finite conic partition.

The tensor calculation proves equality of the additional spectator relation. Full support of the two-dimensional kernels is proved by exponential Fourier decay, analyticity and Fourier uniqueness. The nonlocal relation is not dropped.

Both directions of microlocal solvability are proved for arbitrary distributional solutions with actual compact localization. An explicit projected singular source supplies every finite regularity obstruction.

The full graph transfer retains source order 1-m, exact inverse gain and all smoothing errors. Transported projections are idempotent; orthogonality is not asserted after a nonunitary change. Positive-bracket nonsolvability holds for any prescribed source Sobolev order.

Global symplectic assembly combines these local inverses in the stated properly supported pseudolocal class. The finite-contact companion gives the full operator reduction and the exact favorable and opposite-sign regularity examples.
